places.name: Fort Foster State Historic Site
places.address: U.S. 301, across from Hillsborough River State Park
places.hours_text: Guided fort tours on the 3rd Saturday of each month, November 2026 through April 2027, at 10am and 1pm. The Interpretive Center (Parking Lot 1, Hillsborough River State Park) is open daily 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.

places.summary: A reconstruction of a Second Seminole War fort built in 1836 to guard the bridge over the Hillsborough River, across U.S. 301 from Hillsborough River State Park. You see it on a guided tour; an interpretive center in the park shows artifacts found at the site.
places.quote: Fort Foster was utilized during the Second Seminole War to defend the bridge crossing at the Hillsborough River and served as a resupply point for the soldiers in the field.

heritage.story: Lieutenant Colonel William S. Foster arrived with 430 men on December 1, 1836, and within weeks had built two blockhouses, a large storehouse and a fort to guard the Hillsborough River crossing. The post was abandoned and reactivated several times through the Second Seminole War and was used only for short periods as late as 1849. The fort standing today is a reconstruction that the state built on the site and opened to the public in February 1980; the site was listed on the National Register in 1972.
heritage.visiting: Guided tours only (third Saturdays, November to April), plus living-history events such as Fort Foster Days (February 13–14, 2027). Artifacts from the site are in the Interpretive Center inside Hillsborough River State Park.

places.status_note: The fort itself opens only for guided tours on the third Saturday of each month from November 2026 through April 2027 and for special events, per the Hillsborough River State Park Preservation Society.

places.name: Historic Downtown Plant City
places.summary: Plant City's downtown, a National Register commercial district of 38 historic buildings between Baker and Wheeler Streets and the railroad tracks, with shops and restaurants. The nonprofit Historic Plant City Main Street runs events there, including Last Friday, Oktoberfest and the Strawberry Drop.

designations.name: National Register of Historic Places (Downtown Plant City Commercial District)

heritage.story: Plant City was founded in 1885 as the railroad arrived and was named for railroad builder Henry B. Plant. Its downtown commercial district, bounded by Baker and Wheeler Streets and the railroad tracks, was listed on the National Register of Historic Places on June 8, 1993, with 38 historic buildings. The 1909 Union Depot downtown is now the Robert W. Willaford Railroad Museum.
heritage.visiting: A walkable downtown of shops and restaurants; Historic Plant City Main Street publishes a downtown walking map.

places.notes: Coordinates are the NRHP district point from Wikipedia. Era 'boomtown' from the town's 1885 founding (Visit Tampa Bay) and the 1909 depot; individual building dates are not on the pages read.

places.name: Robert W. Willaford Railroad Museum
places.hours_text: Tuesday-Friday 11:00 AM-4:00 PM; Saturday 10:00 AM-4:00 PM
places.price_text: Free admission; donations appreciated
places.summary: A free railroad museum in historic downtown Plant City, in the 1909 Union Depot, with railroad artifacts, vintage trains and a caboose, and a train viewing platform where you can watch trains pass.

heritage.story: The Plant City Union Depot was built in 1908–1909 for the Atlantic Coast Line and Seaboard Air Line railroads; farmers shipped nearly 4 million quarts of strawberries through it in 1926. Passenger service ended in 1971. When the city threatened to demolish it in 1974, the Plant City Arts Council saved it, and it was added to the National Register in 1975. It reopened as a railroad museum in September 2013 and was named in February 2014 for Robert W. Willaford, who donated 28 railroad items to it.
heritage.visiting: The depot is a free museum Tuesday to Saturday; the train viewing platform sits beside the active tracks.

places.parking_text: Free parking on site and in nearby public lots.

A self-guided walking tour covers the town's historic buildings, and the Dade City Kumquat Festival fills downtown each January.

designations.name: National Register of Historic Places (Pasco County Courthouse)

heritage.story: Dade City was incorporated in 1889 and is the county seat of Pasco County. Its centerpiece is the Pasco County Courthouse, built in 1909 to a design by Georgia architect Edward Columbus Hosford and added to the National Register of Historic Places in 2006. The city's historic register lists more than 150 properties, among them the former Atlantic Coast Line depot, now the Dade City Heritage and Cultural Museum.
heritage.visiting: Walk the downtown streets and the self-guided historic walking tour (the courthouse is stop No. 1); the city publishes walking tour guides and a map of historic properties.

designations.name: National Register of Historic Places (Cortez Historic District)

heritage.story: Cortez, originally known as Hunter's Point, is a fishing village on Sarasota Bay. Its 1912 Cortez Rural Graded Schoolhouse served as a hurricane shelter during the 1921 hurricane, which destroyed much of the village. Residents formed the Cortez Village Historical Society, which placed the village on the National Register of Historic Places in 1995, and the Florida Institute for Saltwater Heritage, which saved about 100 acres along Sarasota Bay.
heritage.visiting: Walk the village with the museum's walking tour brochure; the district is bounded by Cortez Road, 119th Street W, Sarasota Bay and 124th Street Court W. The Florida Maritime Museum (in the schoolhouse) is closed for rehabilitation; the Cortez Cultural Center, 11655 Cortez Road West, opens by appointment with at least 3 days' notice (941-840-0590).

heritage.story: In May 1539 Hernando de Soto landed in the Tampa Bay area with an army of more than 600 soldiers, hired mercenaries, craftsmen and clergy, beginning a four-year, 4,000-mile expedition across the Southeast that met fierce resistance from native peoples protecting their homelands. Congress authorized the memorial at the mouth of the Manatee River on March 11, 1948. Historians do not agree that this was the expedition's actual landing site.
heritage.visiting: Walk the grounds and shoreline trails (dawn to dusk); living history programs are held at Camp Uzita. Entry is free.

places.name: Judah P. Benjamin Confederate Memorial at Gamble Plantation Historic State Park
places.summary: A state park in Ellenton around the antebellum mansion of Major Robert Gamble's sugar plantation, built of tabby in 1845–1850, where likely more than 200 enslaved people lived and worked. The mansion is shown on guided tours; the grounds also hold a large cistern and the 1872 Patten House.
places.quote: This antebellum mansion was home to Major Robert Gamble and is the only surviving plantation house in South Florida.

designations.name: National Register of Historic Places (Robert Gamble House)

heritage.story: After the Second Seminole War, Major Robert Gamble took up 160 acres under the Armed Occupation Act and arrived on the Manatee River in 1844. At its peak his sugar plantation covered 3,500 acres, and likely more than 200 enslaved people lived and worked there; the mansion's columns and two-foot-thick walls are made of tabby. Confederate Secretary of State Judah P. Benjamin sheltered there in May 1865 while evading Union forces. The United Daughters of the Confederacy bought the property and donated it to the state in 1925, and the mansion was listed on the National Register in 1970.
heritage.visiting: The mansion is seen on guided tours; the grounds include a 40,000-gallon cistern and the 1872 Patten House. Tour times and fees are on the Florida State Parks site, which could not be read on Sep 27, 2026.

places.name: Madira Bickel Mound State Archaeological Site
places.summary: A state archaeological site on Terra Ceia Island in northwestern Palmetto, around a flat-topped ceremonial mound of sand, shell and village debris about 20 feet high, raised during some 2,000 years of Native American occupation.
places.quote: The primary feature is a flat-topped ceremonial mound composed of sand, shell and village debris.

heritage.story: Excavations show about 2,000 years of Native American occupation across the Manasota, Weedon Island and Safety Harbor cultures, whose people raised a temple mound about 20 feet high on a base nearly 100 by 170 feet. The Tocobaga kept the mound's ceremonial importance into the sixteenth century. Madira and Karl Bickel donated the land to the state in 1948; it was the first Native American site in Florida designated a State Archaeological Site and was listed on the National Register in 1970.
heritage.visiting: An outdoor mound site run by Florida State Parks; hours were not readable on Sep 27, 2026.

places.summary: A free county-run park of historic buildings in Bradenton covering Manatee County pioneer life from 1840 to 1918, including the county's 1860 courthouse, an 1887 church, the 1903 Wiggins General Store, the 1912 Stephens House, the 1908 Bunker Hill one-room schoolhouse and a 1913 steam engine.

heritage.story: In 1974 women of Manatee United Methodist Church set out to save the congregation's 1887 sanctuary and Manatee County's first courthouse (1860), both slated for demolition. The two buildings were moved to the site in December 1975, and the park opened on July 4, 1976. It has since grown to fourteen structures, including the 1903 Wiggins General Store, the Fogarty Boat Works and the 1908 Bunker Hill schoolhouse.

John Ringling left the estate and his art collection to the State of Florida when he died in 1936; Ca' d'Zan opened to the public in 1946, and Florida State University took over the museum in 2000. heritage.story: In the 1840s Bird Pearson brought his family and enslaved people to a Hernando County homestead and set up a plantation; the Ederington family bought it in 1852 and built the first version of the current house. The Robins family restored the house from 1904, named it Chinsegut Hill and entertained Thomas Edison, J.C. Penney and Helen Keller. In 1932 Raymond and Margaret Robins deeded more than 2,000 acres to the federal government for $1; the University of Florida later held the property and the University of South Florida leased it from 1958 to 2008. Since 2019 the Tampa Bay History Center has run weekend tours with Hernando County.

designations.name: National Register of Historic Places (Crystal River Site)

heritage.story: Native Americans used this bluff on the Crystal River from the second century AD for roughly a thousand years, building a platform mound about 26 feet tall, smaller platform mounds, burial mounds and a shell midden. Activity declined around 1050 as ceremonial life moved downstream to Roberts Island. Clarence B. Moore dug here in 1903 and found copper, mica and shell objects from far away. The state acquired the core mound complex in 1962; it was listed on the National Register in 1970 and designated a National Historic Landmark in 1990.
heritage.visiting: Walk among the mounds and see the museum (Thursday to Monday, 9am–5pm); the grounds open daily 8 am to sunset.

heritage.story: David Levy Yulee, who in 1845 became the first American of Jewish heritage to serve in the U.S. Senate, ran a 5,000-acre plantation on the Homosassa River worked by about 1,000 enslaved African Americans. Its steam-powered mill ran from 1851 to 1864, making sugar, syrup and molasses, and supplied sugar to Confederate soldiers during the Civil War. In May 1864 Union forces burned Yulee's plantation and home but did not find the mill, which was then abandoned and fell into ruin. The site was listed on the National Register in 1970.

Guided walking tours leave daily from the visitor center, next to a Wright-designed Usonian house built in 2013.

designations.name: National Register of Historic Places (Florida Southern College Architectural District)

heritage.story: In 1938 college president Ludd Spivey asked Frank Lloyd Wright to design a campus on an 80-acre former citrus grove above Lake Hollingsworth; Wright first visited on May 8, 1938, and called his vision a "Child of the Sun." He designed 18 structures, and 13 were built, starting with the Annie Pfeiffer Chapel (1938–1941); the E.T. Roux Library went up during World War II with mostly female student labor. The Polk County Science Building, with Wright's only built planetarium, was finished in 1958, the last completed in his lifetime, and a 1939 Usonian house design was finally built in 2013. The district was listed on the National Register in 1975 and designated a National Historic Landmark in 2012.
heritage.visiting: Reservations are suggested at least 24 hours ahead: a 90-minute Basic Tour (10:00 AM and 2:00 PM daily), a 2.5-hour In-Depth Tour (10:30 AM and 1:00 PM daily) and a 20–30 minute Usonian House tour; planetarium shows are ticketed separately. The Behind the Scenes tour is paused.

Casale designed the Polk Theatre as a vaudeville and movie palace that mimics a Mediterranean village, with Italianate walls, faux balconies and a deep blue ceiling of twinkling stars that can simulate sunrise and sunset. report:
# around-daytrips: non-nature attractions Around the Bay and on Day Trips

Checked Sep 27, 2026. 62 `places` records, all in the `around` and `daytrips` regions. Every record's facts come from pages read today (curl text dumps, or WebFetch where curl was blocked). `source_url` is the organization's own page wherever it could be read, otherwise the county's official tourism office (Visit Tampa Bay, Florida's Sports Coast, Bradenton Gulf Islands, Visit Sarasota, Discover Crystal River, Florida's Adventure Coast, Visit Central Florida) or Visit Florida. Wikipedia supplies NRHP reference numbers, build dates and history in `heritage` blocks, always next to an official page.

## Covered (counts by area)

- **plant-city (6):** Dinosaur World; Robert W. Willaford Railroad Museum (1909 Union Depot, heritage); Historic Downtown Plant City (NRHP district, heritage); Parkesdale Market; Keel Farms (winery/cidery, u-pick); Fort Foster State Historic Site (heritage, seasonal tours).
- **lutz-wesley-chapel (5):** Tampa Premium Outlets; The Shops at Wiregrass; Historic Downtown Dade City (1909 courthouse, heritage); Pioneer Florida Museum and Village; Joy-Lan Drive-In.
- **west-pasco (2):** Downtown New Port Richey; West Pasco Historical Society Museum.
- **brandon (2):** Brandon Exchange (ex-Westfield Brandon); Carnival World Museum (International Independent Showmen's Museum, Riverview).
- **temple-terrace (0), apollo-beach (0):** nothing non-nature that justifies a trip (see "Left out").
- **bradenton-anna-maria (15):** De Soto National Memorial (heritage); The Bishop Museum of Science and Nature; Village of the Arts; Bradenton Riverwalk; Anna Maria City Pier (opening-soon); Bridge Street Pier with Historic Bridge Street; Anna Maria Island Historical Museum (seasonal, closed in September); Cortez Historic Fishing Village (heritage); Florida Maritime Museum (temporarily-closed); Manatee Village Historical Park (heritage); Gamble Plantation Historic State Park (heritage); Madira Bickel Mound (heritage); Florida Railroad Museum (Parrish); Ellenton Premium Outlets; Hunsader Farms (seasonal).
- **sarasota (8):** ringling-museum (shared id; includes Ca' d'Zan, heritage); St. Armands Circle; mote-marine-laboratory-aquarium (the new Mote SEA, opened Oct 8, 2025); Historic Spanish Point (heritage); Sarasota Art Museum; Sarasota Jungle Gardens (status to confirm); Sarasota Farmers Market; Big Cat Habitat.
- **nature-coast (7):** Crystal River Archaeological State Park (NHL, heritage); Yulee Sugar Mill Ruins (heritage); Chinsegut Hill (heritage); May-Stringer House / Hernando Heritage Museum (heritage); 1885 Brooksville Train Depot Museum; Old Courthouse Heritage Museum (Inverness); Boyett's Grove.
- **polk (17):** legoland-florida (shared id); Peppa Pig Theme Park; Florida Southern College's Frank Lloyd Wright buildings (NHL, heritage); Ashley Gibson Barnett Museum of Art (id `polk-museum-of-art`, its former name); Fantasy of Flight (seasonal, scaled down); Florida Air Museum; Florida Children's Museum; Polk Theatre (heritage); Historic Downtown Lakeland (Munn Park NRHP district); Spook Hill (NRHP 2019); Polk County History Center (1908 courthouse); Lake Wales History Museum; L.B. Brown House Museum (Black history); Mulberry Phosphate Museum; Homeland Heritage Park; Florida's Natural Grove Store (seasonal Oct-May); Davidson of Dundee.

By kind: museum 20, historic-site 11, shopping 6, historic-district 5, market 3, attraction 3, theme-park 2, pier 2, zoo 2, district 2, and one each of landmark, waterfront, visitor-center, performing-arts, distillery-winery, aquarium. 21 records carry a `heritage` block. Status: open 55, seasonal 5, temporarily-closed 1, opening-soon 1. Signature: ringling-museum, legoland-florida, the Frank Lloyd Wright campus.

## How candidates were found

1. Official tourism listings: Visit Tampa Bay (Plant City page; its listing sitemap grepped for around-the-bay names, which surfaced the renamed Carnival World Museum), Florida's Sports Coast (Pasco), the Bradenton Gulf Islands listing sitemap (615 listings scanned), Visit Sarasota's Things to Do page, Discover Crystal River's historical and museum pages, Florida's Adventure Coast's Historic Sites & Museums page (34 place cards), Visit Central Florida's "50+ Ways" list and its partner sitemap (544 listings scanned).
2. WebSearch by area and kind (Plant City, Pasco, Bradenton/AMI, Polk, Sarasota, Hernando, Citrus) until the session's shared search budget ran out; after that, discovery used the sitemaps above.
3. Wikipedia NRHP articles for reference numbers and dates; the Manatee County Clerk's Historical Resources page (Manatee Village, Florida Maritime Museum); the Anna Maria Island Sun for pier status.
4. Status checks on each place's own page (Helene/Milton notices, construction closures, seasonal calendars).

## Status findings

- Anna Maria City Pier: walkway destroyed by Hurricane Milton (Oct 2024); new walkway finished; the AMI Sun (Sep 16, 2026) expects the pier and the new PIERadise to be fully open before year end (operators hope for November). `opening-soon`.
- Bridge Street Pier (Bradenton Beach): the only one of the island's three piers left standing after 2024; whether its restaurant reopened is unconfirmed. The Rod & Reel Pier was destroyed and is left out.
- Florida Maritime Museum: closed for rehabilitation of its 1912 schoolhouse, no date. `temporarily-closed`.
- De Soto National Memorial: grounds and trails reopened after Helene; the visitor center building was still closed in a March 2025 report; NPS now lists a "Visitor welcome area".
- The Ringling: open; Ca' d'Zan shown on first-floor visits and guided tours while post-2024 restoration continues.
- Mote: the public aquarium is now Mote SEA at 225 University Town Center Drive; City Island is the research campus.
- Fantasy of Flight: scaled down, seasonal Fri-Sun 11-3 on calendar dates; closed on Sep 27. Fort Foster: tours on third Saturdays, Nov 2026-Apr 2027.
- Sarasota Jungle Gardens: conflict. Visit Sarasota lists it as open 363 days a year with hours; the attraction's own homepage still shows an Oct 15, 2024 Milton damage notice asking visitors to watch social media for a reopening date. Kept `open` with a status_note.

## Left out, and why

- Nature places (outdoors slice): TECO Manatee Viewing Center, Bok Tower Gardens, Selby's downtown campus, Weeki Wachee/Buccaneer Bay, Homosassa Springs, Three Sisters, Robinson Preserve, Myakka, Hillsborough River State Park, Bonnet Springs Park, Circle B, Hollis Garden, Siesta Key.
- Event venues (venues-bay): LECOM Park, Joker Marchant Stadium, RP Funding Center, Van Wezel, Sarasota Opera House, Richey Suncoast Theatre, Florida Strawberry Festival grounds. Polk Theatre was kept as a heritage landmark on a day-trip sheet.
- Experiences (exp-land/exp-water): Skydive City, Florida's Giraffe Ranch, Myakka Elephant Ranch, airboats, Cypress Gardens Water Ski Team shows, the Fantasy of Flight biplane ride. Stays: the Hacienda Hotel, LEGOLAND hotels.
- Not verifiable today: Saint Leo Abbey (Cloudflare challenge, WebFetch 403); Sarasota Classic Car Museum (absent from Visit Sarasota's current list, site unreachable; may have closed); Coastal Heritage Museum in Crystal River (its tourism directory page is gone); Pine Avenue (Anna Maria) as its own record (no source beyond "shops along Pine Avenue"); Old Main Street Bradenton and Braden Castle ruins (listings without text); Plant City Photo Archives (a research archive); Zephyrhills Depot Museum, Silver Moon Drive-In, Webb's Candy, Golden Ridge Groves, the Wonder House; Temple Terrace's 1920s Mediterranean Revival neighborhood (no visitable site).

## Open questions for the verifier

1. Sarasota Jungle Gardens: reopened after Milton? If not, set `temporarily-closed`.
2. Anna Maria City Pier: re-check in Oct-Nov 2026 and flip to `open` when the walkway opens.
3. De Soto National Memorial: has the visitor center building reopened?
4. Gamble Plantation, Crystal River Archaeological, Yulee Sugar Mill, Madira Bickel Mound: floridastateparks.org blocks curl and WebFetch (403), so hours, fees and alerts were not read; `url` points at the park pages anyway.
5. Carnival World Museum: showmensmuseum.org returned 503/connection resets all day; hours and admission not recorded.
6. Florida Air Museum posted a "Grand Re-Opening" and an August closure without a year; Polk County History Center's listing mentions a reopening "on July 15" without a year. Both publish regular hours.
7. Ids where another slice may differ: `florida-southern-college-architectural-district`, `polk-museum-of-art` (museum now the Ashley Gibson Barnett Museum of Art), `mote-marine-laboratory-aquarium` (record is Mote SEA), `historic-downtown-dade-city` (the courthouse may appear as `pasco-county-courthouse`), `carnival-world-museum` (a.k.a. International Independent Showmen's Museum).
8. Approximate coordinates: Village of the Arts (a point inside the district, geo_source manual), Florida Children's Museum (Bonnet Springs Park centroid), Homeland Heritage Park (Church Avenue centroid); districts use Wikipedia NRHP points.
9. Process note: research agents share one scratchpad directory. At about 16:56 this agent accidentally ran the exp-land agent's `assemble.py`, which rewrote `research/exp-land/exp-land.json` from that agent's then-empty batches folder. A note was left in the scratchpad and the orchestrator was messaged.


## Verification (2026-09-27)

Adversarial pass by a second agent. **All 62 original records were re-checked** against their source_url (and the pages in also_sources / heritage.sources where a claim rested on them), almost all with WebFetch; a few script-rendered pages were read with curl and grepped (The Shops at Wiregrass, LEGOLAND, Polk Theatre, Polk County History Center listing, Sarasota Jungle Gardens). Coordinates for all 53 records with a street address were re-geocoded in one batch and compared (see "Place"). WebSearch was exhausted for the session, so closure checks and discovery used Bing News RSS via curl, official tourism lists and the organizations' own sites.

### Fixed (46 records changed, plus one notes-only change)

- **Unsupported claims removed or reworded to what the page says:** Fort Foster (garrison dates; reconstruction opened Feb 1980; architect set to null, Foster was the commander); Historic Downtown Plant City (depot is downtown, not a named anchor of the district); Willaford Railroad Museum ("retired locomotive engineer" and "where the tracks crossed" were not on any page; now: named for Willaford, who donated 28 items; museum opened Sep 2013, named Feb 2014); Dade City ("more than 160" historic properties -> more than 150; 1912 depot date dropped); Pioneer Florida Museum (named buildings as the museum lists them); Downtown New Port Richey (amphitheater, splash pad and breweries were not on the pages; "restored" Hacienda dropped); West Pasco museum exhibits; Carnival World Museum (Viking Giant items are boots and a ring, not costumes; "walk-through" wagons dropped); Anna Maria Island Historical Museum (Belle Haven restored 2006; "favorite photo stop" dropped); Bishop Museum ("outdoor science garden" -> interactive space); Cortez ("more than a century" dropped); De Soto (horses/war dogs/enslaved/"generally accepted" claims replaced by the NPS and Wikipedia wording; NRHP listing is "Shaw's Point Archeological District"; heritage.built "1539" removed); Gamble Plantation (Benjamin's "three cabinet posts" and "as a memorial" dropped; style Greek Revival); Madira Bickel ("10-acre" unsupported, removed); Manatee Village (no "Cracker Gothic" or "strawberry school" on the pages: now the 1912 Stephens House and 1908 Bunker Hill schoolhouse; playground is Junior Junction, not train-themed); Village of the Arts (restaurants, not cafes); Sarasota Art Museum ("kunsthalle with no permanent collection" not on the site); Boyett's Grove; 1885 Brooksville Depot (the museum is about the railroad in Brooksville's growth, not "Seminole Wars to settlement"; work car, not box car; source_url moved to the place card that states it); Crystal River Archaeological (no staircase on the pages); Yulee Sugar Mill ("freed the labor force", crops dropped; Union troops did not find the mill); May-Stringer ("overlooking Brooksville" dropped; Stringer's ten-room addition added); Chinsegut (dates per the History Center); FSC Wright campus (WWII female student labor was the Roux Library; tour prices added); Florida's Natural Grove Store; Mulberry Phosphate Museum (**quote removed: not on either page**; exhibits per the tourism listing); AGB Museum; Polk Theatre (films are independent, classic and foreign, Friday to Sunday); Joy-Lan ("first-run" dropped).
- **Hours, prices, phones and urls corrected or filled from the organization's own page:** Parkesdale (Dec-Mar daily, Apr-Nov Wed-Sun), Wiregrass hours, Tampa Premium Outlets quote (full tagline), Brandon Exchange (phone, Dick's House of Sport anchor, 2024 name), Carnival World (IISA phone), Bishop Museum (prices, phone, full holiday list), Historic Spanish Point (prices), Mote SEA (phone; glass-walled labs), Sarasota Art Museum (military free), Sarasota Farmers Market (phone), Hunsader (reopens Oct 1; 2026 Pumpkin Festival dates), Boyett's (hours, phone), Old Courthouse (phone), Davidson of Dundee (own site and hours), Florida Air Museum (full price list, cashless), Florida Children's Museum (own site, hours), Lake Wales History Museum (own site, hours), FSC tours.

Florida Air Museum: the August closure and grand re-opening are **August 2026** (news items dated Jul 27 and Aug 27, 2026). St. Armands Circle: status_note added (WWSB, June 2026: most businesses reopened by fall 2025, some closed for good). Bridge Street Pier: the Anna Maria Oyster Bar lists its Historic Bridge Street Pier restaurant (checked today). Anna Maria City Pier: still opening-soon (AMI Sun, Sep 16, 2026: T-end contract awarded, operators hope for November). De Soto: still unconfirmed whether the visitor center building reopened (NPS hours page last updated Feb 25, 2025).

### Removed

None. No record was closed for good, out of scope, duplicated or unsupported by any page.

### Added (7, each from a page opened today and geocoded with the Census geocoder)

- `bing-rooming-house-museum` (plant-city, heritage, black-history): **temporarily-closed**, the museum's site says closed for Hurricane Milton repairs.
- `zephyrhills-barracks-museum` (lutz-wesley-chapel, heritage): the WWII Zephyrhills Army Airfield infirmary, Saturdays (City of Zephyrhills page).

### Place

The large differences were all bad fallback matches by the re-geocode, not bad records (for example Photon matching "Theatre, South Lake Avenue" for the Polk Theatre, "Sprouts Farmers Market" for the Sarasota Farmers Market, or the Willow end of the Florida Railroad Museum's line).
